candidate_relations.reason: Dysosteosclerosis is a separate sclerosing bone disorder and does not equal the characteristic pycnodysostosis phenotype.
Normal IGF-1 and the osteosclerosis, open fontanel, Wormian bones, and acro-osteolysis indicate a skeletal dysplasia rather than growth hormone deficiency.
Camurati-Engelmann disease primarily causes progressive diaphyseal dysplasia and is not the pycnodysostosis pattern shown here.
Generalized osteosclerosis overlaps with osteopetrosis, but the candidate omits the defining pycnodysostosis diagnosis and its acro-osteolysis and craniofacial pattern.
Achondroplasia and hypochondroplasia cause disproportionate short stature and do not explain diffuse osteosclerosis with acro-osteolysis and an open fontanel.
Pycnodysostosis is a specific sclerosing bone dysplasia, while this label lacks the required subtype.
Cleidocranial dysostosis may cause delayed fontanel closure and Wormian bones but does not account for the characteristic generalized osteosclerosis and distal acro-osteolysis.
Craniodiaphyseal dysplasia is dominated by craniofacial hyperostosis and diaphyseal changes rather than the pycnodysostosis phenotype.
Pseudoachondroplasia produces disproportionate short stature and epiphyseal/metaphyseal abnormalities, not diffuse osteosclerosis with acro-osteolysis.
Sclerosteosis is a distinct hyperostosis syndrome and does not match the open fontanel, Wormian bones, and acro-osteolysis combination of pycnodysostosis.
Osteogenesis imperfecta is characterized by bone fragility and osteopenia rather than diffuse osteosclerosis with distal phalangeal resorption.
Pycnodysostosis belongs to the osteosclerotic/osteopetrosis spectrum, but generic osteopetrosis lacks the required specific diagnosis and characteristic acro-osteolysis phenotype.
Acro-osteolysis is a defining skeletal finding in this case but is only one component of pycnodysostosis.
The '-like syndrome' wording denotes an incompletely specified or potentially distinct mimic and does not establish the exact benchmark diagnosis.
Cathepsin K deficiency is the characteristic cause of pycnodysostosis, but the candidate states the etiology rather than the full clinical diagnostic object.
Pycnodysostosis is a skeletal dysplasia, but this label omits the specific osteosclerosing subtype.
The child has proportionate short stature, but primordial dwarfism does not explain the specific osteosclerosis, open fontanel, Wormian bones, and acro-osteolysis pattern.
Pyknodysostosis is a recognized spelling variant of the benchmark diagnosis and matches the full phenotype.
Acroosteolysis is present in the distal phalanges but is a component finding rather than the complete diagnosis.
Cleidocranial dysplasia can cause persistent fontanels and Wormian bones but does not match the generalized osteosclerosis with acro-osteolysis diagnostic of pycnodysostosis.
